summary.text: In the Sanpoku district of Murakami City, located on the border with Yamagata Prefecture, slash-and-burn fields are planted in mid-August to grow red turnips. Yakibata was one of the primitive farming methods often practiced in mountainous areas where arable land was scarce, but it has declined with the passage of time.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

summary.text: Anbo is a kind of steamed bun with a kneaded dough and filling made of red bean paste, vegetables, etc. It is a local dish in Niigata and northern Nagano prefectures. In some areas, it is called "anbu." "Anbo" look like "oyaki" in Nagano Prefecture, but the main difference is that the skin is made of rice flour instead of wheat flour.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

name.en: Fugunoko-kasuzuke (blowfish roe marinated in sake lees)

summary.text: "Gomafugu" are caught in the Sea of Japan from June to July. The ovaries are salted for two years or more, and then aged for a long time in Sado's sake lees to make "Fugunoko-kasuzuke." In Niigata Prefecture, it is unique to Sado, and similar processed products exist in Ishikawa and Fukui prefectures. It is said to have been made on Sado Island since the Edo period.Fugu processing requires a special license, a Fugu Chef's License.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

summary.text: Niigata Prefecture, the largest consumer of eggplant in Japan, has a local dish called "Fukashi Nasu (steamed eggplant). In some areas, it is called "Nasu Bukashi. In the Niigata style, steamed eggplants are cooled in a refrigerator and dipped in soy sauce mixed with Japanese mustard. It is also eaten by hand breaking pieces off and dipped in ginger soy sauce or Pon-zu (soy sauce with Japanese citrus juice).Niigata Prefecture boasts the nation's largest eggplant acreage (2019) and grows many varieties of eggplant.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

summary.text: Hegisoba is a type of cut buckwheat noodle made with seaweed called funori as a binder and served in a wooden tray called a hegi. It is a local dish said to have originated in the Uonuma region, born from the fusion of Niigata Prefecture's textile culture and soba food culture. The "hegi" in hegisoba refers to a square tray made of stripped wooden pieces, and is derived from the Japanese word "hegu," which is a pun on the word "hagu" meaning to peel.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

name.kana: ひやししるみそじたて

summary.text: “Hiyashi-shiru-Miso-jitate” (Chilled soup with Miso) is a cold soup seasoned with dashi (Japanese soup stock) and miso, and eaten mainly in summer. It has been eaten as a local dish in various parts of Japan since ancient times. The name and ingredients used vary from prefecture to prefecture, including Yamagata, Saitama, and Miyazaki prefectures.Miyazaki Prefecture's “Hiya-jiru” is made with fish, such as grilled and shredded horse mackerel, or small dried sardines, sesame and barley miso, and served over rice, or barley rice.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

summary.text: In the Niigata prefecture where it snows heavily, 「pickled dried daikon radish」is a preserved food made to last throughout the winter. A representative dish of the Joetsu region, it is also known as 「hari hari pickles」due to the crunchy ‘hari hari’ sound it makes when eating it. However, the Niigata prefecture’s 「pickled dried daikon」 is slightly different from the「hari hari pickles 」found in other prefectures as it doesn’t use vinegar.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

summary.text: Igoneri" is a local dish representative of Sado Island, made from the Japanese rush grass harvested from the Sea of Japan. It was made in every household from fall to winter. Igogusa is a type of seaweed that grows on large seaweed such as kombu and hondawara, and is widely used mainly on the Sea of Japan side. It is called "igo" in the Sado region and "ego" in the Niigata region. It is made by boiling and kneading sun-dried dried sea weed while adjusting the amount of water, then spreading it thinly and cooling it down to harden it.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

summary.text: Gosen City, where the Agano and Hayade Rivers flow through, is blessed with fertile, well-drained soil and abundant water, which nurtures many prefectural brand vegetables. Among them, along with "Gosenbijin (lotus root)" and "Yawahada Negi (leek)," the Kinu Otome taro is a major product in Gosen City. In Gosen-shi, taro has long been grown by farmers as their own vegetable, and now boasts the largest production in Niigata Prefecture (according to the Gosen-shi website, 2048).
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

summary.text: Iizushi, a type of narezushi (matured sushi) that has been handed down from generation to generation in Murakami City, originated as a preserved food. It is a local dish made by marinating thin slices of salmon, herring roe, carrots, daikon radish, salmon roe, hizu (cartilaginous part of the tip of the nose of salmon), and yuzu in rice and koji (malt) and fermenting it. The slow fermentation at low temperatures gives the koji a mild sourness, aroma, and sweetness. Salt-dried salmon, a specialty of Murakami City, is used.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

summary.text: “Kakiae namasu” is a local dish that uses reddish-purple edible chrysanthemums. The custom of eating chrysanthemum flowers is unique to the culture of the Tohoku region as well as Niigata Prefecture, and it is said that people began eating chrysanthemum flowers around the Edo period. Kakinomoto is a chrysanthemum called Enmeiraku, which has long been cultivated in the gardens of farmers and in the corners of fields in Niigata Prefecture. It is characterized by its unique aroma, crunchy texture, and sweetness.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

summary.text: Kanzuri, a traditional fermented seasoning from Myoko City (formerly Arai City) in Niigata Prefecture, is also written in Japanese characters meaning “made in the cold” because it is made on the coldest day of the year. It is said that Kenshin Uesugi, a military commander in the Sengoku period, brought in the precious chili peppers from Kyoto and distributed them to farmers. It was initially made simply by mixing ground chili pepper with miso. Myoko City is located in the Joetsu region of Niigata Prefecture, adjacent to Nagano Prefecture.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

summary.text: Kensan-yaki is a local dish of grilled rice balls topped with ginger miso or sweet miso. It is also called "kensashi-yaki," "kenshin-yaki," or "kensayaki." The name is said to have originated when Kenshin Uesugi used to eat rice balls that had become cold and tough by stabbing them with the tip of his sword as food for his soldiers during war. In the old days, transportation was not well developed, so people had to travel on foot along snow-covered roads when returning to their hometowns.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

summary.text: Kiri-zai" is a local dish from the Uonuma region, made by mixing natto with chopped vegetables. The "kiri-zai" in kiri-zai means "to cut" and "zai" means "dai" in vegetable. Kirizai has a long history, and there is a record that during the Warring States period, samurai warriors used to carry kirizai as food for their troops.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

summary.text: “Kujira-jiru” is a local dish consisting of salted whale blubber, and vegetables, simmered in miso. Because of the influence of Kitamae-bune, various cultures of other places have taken root in Niigata, and “Kujira-jiru” is one of them. Once upon a time, whales caught in western Japan were salted and transported to Niigata by Kitamae-bune.Whale fat is high in unsaturated fatty acids, which are considered to be good for health. In Niigata, whale fat was eaten as a stamina food, especially during the hot midsummer season.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

summary.text: Fu is a processed food whose main ingredient is gluten and is made by kneading wheat flour with water.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

name.ja: 身欠きにしんの糀漬け
name.kana: みがきにしんのこうじづけ
name.zh_tw: 身欠きにしんの糀漬け

summary.text: Hokkaido herring occupied a major position among the goods carried by the Kitamae-bune (northern-bound ships) because it did not last long in its raw state. In the days when refrigeration technology was not yet developed, herring was removed from its entrails and head, dried, and processed into fertilizer, fish oil, and other products before being transported to various regions on the Kitamae-bune.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

summary.text: The number of sardines, caught has been decreasing in recent years, but in the past, a large number of sardines were caught in April and May along the coast of the Sea of Japan. The gills and innards of the sardines were removed and marinated in a large amount of salt, to make "Shokkara-Iwashi“."Shokkara-Iwashi" is a kind of Japanese anchovy, made from 90 sardines, and one sho (1.5kg) of Salt.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

summary.text: Nina is a local dish made by boiling salted vegetable leaves and was eaten as a common household dish in Niigata Prefecture. Taina is mainly used. Taina was introduced from China in the early Meiji period and was bred to be adapted to Niigata. It is widely used as one of the Nagaoka vegetables. Depending on the region, nozawana or radish leaves are used as well. Nozawana is used in the Uonuma and Joetsu regions.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

summary.text: Nokpe" is a typical Niigata home-style dish and a local delicacy found throughout Japan. Unlike "Nogei-jiru" found throughout the country, Niigata's "Nogpe" is more of a stew than a soup. The main ingredient is taro, and vegetables and mushrooms are simmered in a light flavor and thickened with saya-endo (pea pods) as the green seasoning. In winter, when saya-endo is unavailable, "to-tomame" is sprinkled on top of the taro. Totto-mame" are salmon roe.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

summary.text: "Sado no Nishime" is a local dish eaten on Sado City in Niigata Prefecture, where broth is made from grilled flying fish and ingredients such as vegetables, kombu(=kelp), and grilled tofu are slowly simmered over a long period of time. Oden-style nishime is well seasoned and delicious. In some areas, pollack, squid, and fu are added. It is called "nishime" because it is boiled until there is no liquid left, and has been enjoyed by the islanders as a long-standing family favorite.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

summary.text: The Miomote River, where salmon run upstream, flows through Murakami City, which is known as “Salmon City,” and in autumn, the city is filled with salmon. It is said that there are more than 100 cooking methods in Murakami City, where the culture of eating salmon carefully from head to tail has taken root. One of these salmon dishes is “salmon yakizuke” . As the name suggests, it is a simple dish in which grilled salmon is marinated in soy sauce mixed with sake and mirin and served as is or broiled.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

summary.text: In Niigata Prefecture, there is a simple and rustic tasting " Sankaku Chimaki" that is rare in Japan. It is a simple chimaki made of glutinous rice wrapped in bamboo leaf, folded into a triangular shape, tied with igusa (=rush), and boiled slowly in plenty of hot water for two hours. It is served with kinako (￢￢=soybean flour) sprinkled on top. Although slightly less well known than sasa dango, chimaki is said to be the oldest chimaki in Japan.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

summary.text: Sasa-dango, a well-known specialty of Niigata, is a bale-shaped dumpling wrapped in bamboo leaves and tied with a string of sedge or other material. It has been eaten in the Chuetsu and Shimoetsu regions of Niigata and parts of the Aizu region of Fukushima Prefecture for about 500 years. It is said that "Kenshin Uesugi used it as a portable food" because it was considered a portable preserved food in the Warring States period, as bamboo leaves have a sterilizing effect. It is also said that it was used as a portable food by Uesugi Kenshin.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

summary.text: "Sasazushi" is a traditional local dish from the Hokushinetsu region., In Niigata Prefecture, it is mainly enjoyed in the Joetsu region. While a similar dish in Ishikawa Prefecture called "Oshizushi" is made by pressing down on vinegared rice wrapped in bamboo leaves, Niigata's "Sasazushi" is made by placing vinegared rice on kuma bamboo leaves and arranging various ingredients and seasonings on top.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

summary.text: Shoyu Okowa" is a local dish of Nagaoka City that is colored with soy sauce. It is a local dish characterized by the inclusion of fluffy cooked kidney beans. It is not red like ordinary sekihan, but brown because it is colored with soy sauce. It is eaten only in Nagaoka City and its vicinity, and for those who grew up in this area, sekihan has been flavored with soy sauce since childhood.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

summary.text: In the mountainous regions of Niigata Prefecture, young shoots of Chishimazasa bamboo called "Hime-takenoko" are harvested from late May to early July. In the Joetsu region of Niigata Prefecture and the Hokushin region of Nagano Prefecture, when hime-takenoko are available, they are made into bamboo shoot soup and eaten. In addition to the bamboo shoots and canned mackerel, the Joetsu region often adds potatoes, carrots, onions, daikon radish, fried thin tofu, and other ingredients to the soup, which is then simmered with an egg.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

name.en: Tare Katsu Don (Sauced BBQ Pork Bowl)

summary.text: "Tare Katsu Don" is a dish where freshly fried thin pork cutlets are placed on top of rice and drizzled with a sweet and savory soy-based sauce. It doesn't include a scrambled egg topping. This simple dish features a unique characteristic of having two or more cutlets placed on a single bowl. The pork used in this dish is thinner than the typical pork cutlet found in other katsudon dishes, and it is coated with a light batter.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

summary.text: In the mountains, many wild vegetables are harvested in the springtime. It is said that wild vegetables grown under the snow are tastier and less bitter because when the snow melts, the acidity of the plants is removed. Zenmai or flowering fern is one of them, and when harvested in early spring and hung in the sun to dry, it was an especially useful as a preserved food in the wintertime. Since it can be used in a variety of ways, even stewing, Zenmai is indispensable food in Niigata prefecture.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

summary.text: "Zuiki" refers to the petiole (stalk) of a type of taro called "Yatsugashira." It is a summer vegetable that has been enjoyed in various regions across the country for a long time. In Niigata, it is cultivated extensively in the Shinano River basin and paddy field areas. Harvesting starts as early as June and continues until September. It is designated as Nagaoka vegetables, Joetsu vegetables, and Kashiwazaki vegetables.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）
